record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: If Ω ⊂ C is an arclength null-quadrature domain, must Ω admit a roof function, meaning a positive harmonic function u on Ω whose gradient ∇u agrees along ∂Ω with the inward-pointing unit normal vector?

evidence.quote: Here, by a roof function, we mean a positive function u harmonic in Ω such that the gradient ∇u coincides with the inward-pointing unit normal vector along ∂Ω.
Question: Does every ALNQD admit a roof function?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}$ be an unbounded domain with rectifiable boundary $\partial\Omega$. Call $\Omega$ an arclength null-quadrature domain (ALNQD) if for every function $f$ that is analytic in $\Omega$, continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$, and integrable with respect to arclength on $\partial\Omega$, one has $\int_{\partial\Omega} f\, ds = 0$. A roof function on $\Omega$ is a positive harmonic function $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ that extends continuously to $\partial\Omega$ with $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$, and whose gradient $\nabla u$ coincides along $\partial\Omega$ with the inward-pointing unit normal vector to $\partial\Omega$ (equivalently, $u$ vanishes on $\partial\Omega$ and $\partial u/\partial n = 1$ on $\partial\Omega$, where $n$ is the inward unit normal).

Question: Does every arclength null-quadrature domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}$ admit a roof function?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been partially resolved: Khavinson and Lundberg established that every arclength null-quadrature domain with finitely many boundary components admits a roof function (Bull. London Math. Soc., 2022; arXiv:2005.09822). The general case (without a finiteness assumption on the boundary components) does not appear to be settled.

status_evidence.title: A note on arclength null quadrature domains
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the existence of a roof function for arclength null quadrature domains having finitely many boundary components.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a roof function is proved under the assumption of finitely many boundary components, leaving the general case unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A note on arclength null quadrature domains - Bull. London Math. Soc.
status_evidence.snippet: Khavinson and Lundberg, 2022; existence of roof function for ALNQDs with finitely many boundary components.
status_evidence.claim: Published resolution of the finite-boundary-component case.
